To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the soil N min concentrations in spring in Lithuania's soils are affected by the soil texture and the climatic conditions of the previous winter.
the soil N min concentrations in spring in Lithuania's soil regions are influenced by the crop and pre-crop, soil texture, and climatic factors.
the soil N min distribution in the 0–60 soil layer in spring is affected by soil texture, crops, pre-crops, winter air temperature, precipitation and their interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the soil N min concentrations in the Lithuanian soils, which are important indicators of the state of the environment and agricultural land.
the assessment of the long-term fluctuating dynamics of soil N min concentration as affected by the geographical and climatic conditions.
the long-term monitoring of N min concentration in Lithuanias soils in spring and its spatial variability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the soil N min concentrations in spring in Lithuanian agricultural fields were within the range of 20–80 mg N min /kg soil in 0–30 cm soil layer and 10–60 mg N min / kg soil in 30–60 cm layer.
the soil N min concentrations in Lithuania in spring are not only affected by the climatic and soil factors, but also by the agricultural factors.
soil N min concentrations in 0– 60 cm soil layer were the lowest in the fields where perennial grasses were cultivated, in sandy loams, and in the fields where pre-crop was spring cereals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the soil N min concentrations are the lowest when perennial grass fields and spring cereals or spring rape are cultivated in sandy loam, sand or clay soils, when precipitation during the winter months is high (above 200 mm), when the predominant winter air temperatures are above 0°C and when the soil texture is sandy.
the soil N min distribution in spring is affected by the local soil and climatic conditions, the type and rotation of crops and the level of precipitation during winter.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the soil N min concentrations in spring are affected not only by climatic conditions, but also by soil texture, crop and pre-crop types.
the soil N min level is not uniform across the territory of Lithuania.
